headline: Rocky Mountain Corridor Protects Wildlife at Continental Scale
meta_description: A 2,100-mile conservation corridor across the Rocky Mountains has protected 24 million acres and built over 200 wildlife crossings since 1997.
summary_short: The Yellowstone to Yukon Conservation Initiative is creating an enormous connected habitat across the Rocky Mountains for safe wildlife migration.
body:
Since 1997, an ambitious conservation project spanning the entire Rocky Mountain range has been quietly reshaping how we think about protecting wildlife. The Yellowstone to Yukon Conservation Initiative (Y2Y) aims to build a continuous 2,100-mile corridor that allows animals to migrate safely across fragmented lands. Already, the effort has protected more than 24 million acres of habitat and supported the construction of over 200 wildlife crossings—physical infrastructure that lets creatures move between separated ecosystems without the fatal risks of highways and other human development.

The project's scale reflects a growing understanding that habitat loss alone isn't wildlife's only threat. Fragmentation—the breaking apart of connected landscapes by roads, dams, and development—can isolate populations and prevent the natural movement essential for healthy ecosystems. By coordinating among several governments and countless smaller conservation projects, Y2Y addresses both problems at once, creating what amounts to a protected superhighway for everything from grizzly bears to lynx across one of North America's most vital mountain ranges.

The initiative joins other creative solutions gaining momentum. In California, a massive wildlife overpass is being built across the 101 Freeway to reconnect severed habitats. These projects prove that when we recognize fragmentation as the problem it is, we can engineer real solutions. Y2Y's progress over nearly three decades shows that thinking big about wildlife protection—and doing the unglamorous work of coordination and long-term commitment—can yield transformative results measured in millions of acres and hundreds of safe passages.
quick_facts: 24 million acres of habitat protected since 1997
Over 200 wildlife crossings built to date
